case_title: Kilakkatha Parambath Sasi & Ors. v. State of Kerala
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (basis of conviction); charged under IPC ss.147, 148, 307, 324 and 302 r/w s.149
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured witness PW-1 and independent witnesses PW-2, PW-3, PW-4); medical (post-mortem by PW-7 and injury examination by PW-8); investigation records (FIR, trip-sheet recovered by IO)
aggravating_circumstances: Deceased had 58 injuries, most incised and cutting wounds, some of huge dimensions; attack by a group armed with sword, axe and knife
high_court_outcome: Appeal against acquittal allowed in part: four appellants convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment; acquittal of other three maintained
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 r/w s.34
neutral_facts: The victim and his brother were travelling on a bus with several other passengers. The victim alleged that when the bus reached a stop, two of the accused shouted that they would be killed and pushed the victim and his brother out onto the road. Other accused then ran from a nearby shop carrying a sword, an axe and a long knife and inflicted injuries on both men. The attack was said to be linked to political animosity between the two groups, with the accused described as belonging to one political party and the victim and his brother to the other. The victim's brother was taken to hospital in a critical condition, was referred to a medical college and died there. The victim was admitted to a government hospital. Police reached the scene about an hour after the incident. The police recorded the victim's statement at the hospital in the evening, and a formal report was registered later that evening. The post-mortem found 58 injuries on the deceased, most of them incised and cutting wounds, some of large size. The victim was found to have three incised wounds. The prosecution relied on the victim as an injured eyewitness, on two passengers who were on the bus, and on an independent auto-rickshaw driver who said he had come to the stop for repairs. The investigating officer recovered the bus trip-sheet, but the bus crew were not examined as witnesses.
physical_harm: Deceased died after 58 injuries, mostly incised and cutting wounds; PW-1 (the victim's brother) sustained three incised wounds and grievous injuries
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court. The prosecution alleged the accused formed an unlawful assembly, but the court made no finding of premeditation or planning
motive: alleged: political animosity between BJP workers (accused) and Congress workers (victims)
key_evidence_accepted: Injured eyewitness PW-1's testimony; eyewitness testimony of PW-2, PW-3 and PW-4; the spontaneity of the FIR; post-mortem and injury evidence of the doctors
witness_credibility: PW-1 (injured witness) found credible and present. PW-4 found a truly independent witness with no reason to discard his statement. PW-2 accepted as present despite not being named in the FIR. PW-3 gave a categoric statement. Trial court's doubts on these witnesses were rejected
trial_duration: offence: 24 March 1994; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 23.05.2003; Supreme Court: 4 February 2011
legal_representation: Accused/appellants: U.R. Lalit (senior counsel), E.M.S. Anam, Fazlin Anam. State of Kerala: Dinesh Dwivedi, G. Prakash, Beena Prakash, V. Senthil
investigation_status: FIR registered on the victim's statement recorded at the hospital; post-mortem conducted; investigation completed; accused charged
procedural_irregularity: Bus crew not examined although the investigating officer recovered the trip-sheet; the court held this did not defeat the prosecution case. Trial court's finding of FIR delay was rejected as farfetched
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted all seven accused. High Court: acquittal reversed for four appellants, convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 and sentenced to life; acquittal of three others maintained. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: High Court interference was justified because the trial judgment was perverse; there was no FIR delay; the injured PW-1's presence could not be doubted; the three unnamed accused had been acquitted and were not before the Court
defence_argument: Unexplained FIR delay allowed fabrication and involvement of innocent persons; eyewitness accounts were discrepant and contradicted by medical evidence; presence of PWs 2, 3 and 4 was doubtful; bus crew were not examined; no ground to interfere with the acquittal
legal_principle_applied: Appellate court should not interfere with acquittal save in exceptional cases, and only if the trial findings are not borne out by evidence and are perverse; but the High Court may re-appraise evidence and must interfere if the trial findings were not possible on the evidence
precedent_relied_upon: Arulvelu and Anr. v. State represented by the Public Prosecutor and Anr. (2009) 10 SCC 206
